inputs.share_count_basis: POST 2-for-1 split (effective 2026-07-01). 907,200,000 issued less 2,442,006 treasury at 2026-06-30 (H1 FY2026 tanshin, restated for the split) = 904,757,994. No dilutive securities: diluted EPS is shown as '-' in the tanshin. Held FLAT because SBC (immaterial) is expensed in the flows; FY2025's JPY80bn buyback retired 12.3m pre-split shares and is the mechanism that keeps the count flat, not a separate value driver.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual securities report, cash-flow statement share-based payment expense JPY641m; equity-award taxes nil (Kao settles awards with treasury shares, no net-share-settlement withholding line). Immaterial at 0.04% of revenue but kept explicit per house rule.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built: 10y JGB ~1.7% + Japan ERP ~5.5% x beta ~0.65 for a net-cash household/personal-care staple gives a cost of equity near 5.3-5.6%; the house JPY reference is ~9% for cyclical keiretsu suppliers. 7.0% is used as a deliberate cushion above the CAPM figure and well below the industrial reference, because Kao is defensive (repeat-purchase staples, 57% Japan, net cash JPY194bn) but not immune to raw-material and China cycles. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged in the flows (scenario paths and weights), not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. FY2025 lease principal repayments JPY22,281m (financing, FY2025 AR cash-flow statement) plus interest on lease liabilities JPY1,943m (note 17) = JPY24.2bn = 1.43% of revenue, charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (JPY104.9bn at 2026-06-30) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is bonds and borrowings only. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 depreciation and amortisation JPY85,841m less ROU depreciation JPY19,302m = JPY66,539m = 3.94% of revenue. Short-term lease expense (JPY1.9bn) is already inside EBITDA and is not charged again.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; non-controlling interests deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at book value (JPY30,091m at 2026-06-30). NCI's profit share is small (JPY505m of JPY120,586m FY2025 net income; JPY2,607m FY2024), so deducting book is the conservative side of the two treatments.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: non-US operating consumer company, owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md read; adaptations a1 currency-matched WACC, b lease treatment B, c NCI in bridge, d interest income stripped against net cash in bridge, e SBC-near-zero market, f risk charged once). First valuation of this ticker. FY0 = FY2025 (last completed year, 31 Dec 2025); year 1 = FY2026 at the August-2026 raised guidance (revenue JPY1,800bn, operating income JPY190bn). Balance sheet and share count are the LATEST filing (H1 FY2026, 30 June 2026), ten months into year 1; the overlap is immaterial because net cash was flat between FY2025 (JPY191.6bn) and H1 FY2026 (JPY194.3bn). last_fcf follows the contract formula (reported FCF 128,835 - SBC 641 - interest income 3,286 = 124,908); the forward build additionally charges lease cash of ~1.4% of revenue, so the FY2025 like-for-like owner FCF after lease principal is JPY102.6bn (6.1% of revenue) and the year-1 component build lands at ~6.9%, consistent with a lower working-capital drag than FY2025. Interest income stripped because net cash (JPY194bn) exceeds the FCF base. Investment securities / cross-shareholdings are NOT added to the bridge (their dividend income is not in the EBITDA-based flows either): an unmodelled, modest upside. SBC-near-zero: house and street bases coincide to within JPY1/share; the band collapses, band_position is not meaningful. Share basis is post-split throughout; all pre-FY2026 EPS in the Metrics CSV is pre-split (x2 to compare). IFRS 18 adopted FY2026 restates operating-income presentation; the EBITDA margin anchor (FY2025 14.8%, H1 FY2026 16.1%) is read on the restated basis. All money inputs in JPY millions (CSV scale); shares in millions, so per-share values are in JPY. Price: Yahoo regular close; no after-hours volatility flag. Working capital: manufacturer with receivables + inventory > payables, so growth consumes cash (wc_capture negative).

equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 balance sheet, 2026-06-30; flows are consolidated, so NCI is deducted once here (adaptations c)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (2.9%), cross-checked against revenue 5yr 4.1%; the base path starts at FY2026 guidance (+6.6%) and decelerates to 2%, averaging ~3.1% over ten years
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 2.9% vs revenue 5yr 4.1% (30% relative gap, borderline) and EPS 5yr -0.2% (FY2020 was a COVID hygiene-demand peak and FY2023 carried the Cosmetics impairment, so the EPS endpoints distort; 3yr EPS +12.4% is the recovery off that trough). Equity growth is held back by payout: dividends ~JPY70bn/yr plus the FY2025 JPY80bn buyback against ~JPY120bn net income.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs on pre-split EPS (FY2020 262.25 -> FY2025 260.30). Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income across the whole history: FY2020 143.4bn (SBC recorded as -0.4bn in the CSV, treated as nil), FY2022 51.4bn (raw-material squeeze trough), FY2025 124.9bn. SBC is immaterial, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs are within 1pp of each other; the 3yr figure is a trough-to-recovery artefact, not a trend. FCF has not grown over five years while revenue compounded 4%: FY2020 was a hygiene-demand windfall year (OCF JPY214.7bn) and FY2025 absorbed working-capital build.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = FY2026 guidance JPY1,800bn (+6.6%; H1 was +7.8%). Thereafter price/mix-led low-single-digit growth: Japan (~57% of sales) flat-to-1% volume plus periodic price pass-through, Asia/Europe mid-single-digit, Chemical tied to industrial demand. Decelerates to 2% by year 8, above the 1.5% terminal to reflect the 43% overseas mix.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 EBITDA margin 14.8% (OI 164.1 + D&A 85.8 on 1,688.6); H1 FY2026 16.1%; FY2026 guidance OI JPY190bn + ~JPY88bn D&A = 15.4%, and H1 suggests the guidance is conservative, so Y1 15.6%. Ramps to 17.0% (OI margin ~12%) by year 7 as the K27 Cosmetics reform and ROIC discipline mature; FY2019 pre-reform peak was 19.6%, so 17% leaves headroom and does not assume the 2030+ Cosmetics 15% OI target is met in full.
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 capex JPY70.8bn = 4.2% of revenue; FY2026 plan ~JPY91bn INCLUDING right-of-use additions (~JPY20bn/yr), i.e. ~JPY71bn ex-ROU = 3.9-4.1%. ROU additions are carried by the lease line, not capex. D&A ex-ROU 3.9% roughly equals capex: the asset base is mature.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 effective rate 29.0% (49,260 / 169,846). Cash taxes paid FY2023-FY2025 (24.6-31.0bn) were depressed by the FY2023 Cosmetics impairment year; H1 FY2026 cash tax JPY34.3bn shows the benefit has run off. 29% flat, no shelter perpetuated.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer with receivables + inventories > payables; each JPY100 of revenue growth absorbs ~JPY5 of working capital. Deferred revenue (JPY43bn) is stable, not a growth tailwind.

bull.rationale: Cosmetics reform delivers: six focus brands reach ~JPY400bn sales at a 15% OI margin after 2030, Health & Beauty Care keeps premiumising, ASEAN/India cosmetics expansion lands, Chemical specialty mix lifts margins. Group EBITDA margin returns to the FY2019 peak (19.6%) by year 10; growth stays mid-single-digit for five years. Same WACC as base: the upside is in the flows.

bear.rationale: FY2026 lands near guidance (H1 already banked) then a FY2021-22-style squeeze: palm oil / petrochemical inflation and tariff-driven procurement costs outrun price pass-through, Japanese consumers trade down, Merries and Cosmetics lose further share in China to local brands, and the Cosmetics reform slips as the 2018-2023 one did. EBITDA margin settles at 13.5% (between the FY2021 16.3% and FY2022 12.9% troughs); revenue grows 1% nominal. Not a solvency case: net cash and a JPY70bn dividend remain.

scenario_narratives.base: K27 keeps delivering what it has since FY2024: price/mix in Fabric & Home Care, a Cosmetics business that is profitable again (OI JPY10.4bn FY2025 from -3.7bn) but still well short of its 2030+ ambitions, and a Chemical business tracking industrial demand. Revenue follows the raised FY2026 guidance then compounds 2-4% on price/mix; EBITDA margin climbs from 14.8% to 17% over seven years (OI margin ~12%), short of the FY2019 peak. Capex and lease spend hold at ~5.5% of revenue combined; the JPY194bn net cash funds buybacks that keep the count flat.
scenario_narratives.bull: The September-2025 Cosmetics overhaul under Uchiyama repeats her Hair Care turnaround: SENSAI, Molton Brown, Kanebo, Sofina, Curel and KATE scale internationally, ASEAN/India expansion lands, and group EBITDA margin returns to the ~19.5% FY2019 level by year 10 while revenue compounds 4-5% for five years. Chemical specialty mix adds a point of margin. Terminal growth 2% reflects a larger overseas share.
scenario_narratives.bear: Raw-material and tariff cost inflation outruns pricing (as in FY2021-22, when EBITDA margin fell from 18.9% to 12.9%), Japanese volumes soften under consumer price sensitivity, China sanitary and cosmetics demand keeps eroding to local brands, and the Cosmetics reform stalls at break-even. EBITDA margin settles at 13.5%, revenue grows ~1% nominal, terminal growth 1%. Balance sheet unimpaired; the downside is a de-rating of a 25x-earnings staple, not distress.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 20/50/30. Bull trimmed because it needs several independent things to go right (Cosmetics turnaround that has slipped before, sustained price pass-through in a price-sensitive Japan, China share stabilisation) to reach a margin the company last earned pre-COVID. Bear lifted modestly for raw-material/tariff exposure and China, but held at 20% because the bear is margin compression on a net-cash balance sheet, not solvency; the FY2024-FY2026 margin trajectory and H1 FY2026 beat argue against weighting it higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a JPY-built 7% WACC with risk carried in three scenario paths rather than the discount rate. SBC is immaterial so house and street coincide; leases are charged as operating cost (treatment B) and excluded from net debt; NCI deducted once at book; interest income stripped and the JPY194bn net cash added once in the bridge. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon and 20x year-10 FCF; at 7%/1.5% Gordon (~18.5x) binds.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly JPY180-200/share; the base assumes 17% against a 14.8% FY2025 actual and a 19.6% FY2019 peak
Raw-material (palm oil, petrochemical) and tariff cost cycles with lagged price pass-through, the mechanism behind the FY2021-23 margin collapse
Cosmetics reform execution: the 2030+ JPY400bn / 15% OI target is not in the base and is the main bull driver
China demand and local-brand competition in Merries and Cosmetics
JPY translation of the ~43% overseas sales base; WACC built in JPY so a weaker yen flatters flows but not the discount rate
Terminal-value share of EV is high (~60%) for a low-growth, low-WACC staple, so the valuation is sensitive to the WACC/g pair; see sensitivity grid

Unmodelled: investment securities and cross-shareholdings are not in the bridge (modest upside); the FY2026 overlap between FY0 flows and the June-2026 balance sheet is immaterial because net cash was flat
